verify.note:
Independently reproduced every material claim in this finding from scratch.

1) Reran the exact command on the real project (ssh reyerchu@192.168.1.120, ~/.claude/plugins/cache/vibe-ic-marketplace/vibe-ic/1.6.71-pr427/programs/flow_compliance_check.py against ~/campaign_pr427/spm/converge_ihp-sg13g2 with `--flow phase1_phase2_phase3 --skip-analog --skip-hardware`). 2) Read flow_compliance_check.py directly: lines 6529 and 6534 are exactly `failing = [r for r in ... if r.status == "FAIL"]` (the P0-structural-only branch and the normal branch respectively). Traced `ok` (line 6558-6562) and `overall` (6715-6720): only `failing`, `missing`, and `setup_required_skipped` gate the verdict. `counts["SKIPPED-CONDITION"]` is used in exactly two places in the whole file (line 6570, subtracted from `total_required`; line 6582, cosmetic summary string) and never touches `ok`/`overall`. So a SKIPPED-CONDITION step categorically cannot, by itself, produce Overall:FAIL — confirmed by direct code read, not paraphrase.

3) Checked the actual live run's Overall: it prints `FAIL` — but only because Step P0 (an unrelated structural-RTL gate, provenance_output_hash_completeness_check) also FAILed in this snapshot. This does NOT refute the finding: the finding's claim is about the mechanism ("would not, by itself, prevent"), which is a structural property of the code that I verified directly, independent of what else happens to be failing in this particular snapshot. If P0 were clean, this run's Overall would resolve to PASS_WITH_WAIVERS (WAIVED=2 for the two --skip-hardware FPGA steps) with the DFT gap completely unflagged at the top-line verdict.

4) Confirmed the yaml's stated intent: phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml lines 745-748 and 766-770 explicitly say the foundry-bar DFT gate 'FAILs honestly ... never a vacuous pass' for exactly the OSS-tool-limited case. But dft_signoff_check.py lines 320-349 contain an explicit carve-out: when a sibling sentinel honestly self-reports the ATPG-couldn't-measure capability gap, the checker returns rc=2 (a documented 'VACUOUS_PASS/SKIPPED-CONDITION' convention, confirmed at flow_compliance_check.py:1823/1866) instead of the FAIL its own docstring promises. design_one_shot_runner.py:9519-9563 shows this is deliberate, well-commented code (labeled 'HONEST disclosed capability-gap'), not an accident — but its effect is exactly what the finding describes.

But that promotion path only fires when the step lands in `failing`/`missing` AND `overall == "FAIL"` first (line 6742). Because the #608/#675 self-skip sentinel converts Step 11 to SKIPPED-CONDITION upstream of that check, it never reaches the FAIL/MISSING bucket at all — so it also bypasses the codebase's OWN existing safety net for this exact scenario, landing as a silent bare PASS/PASS_WITH_WAIVERS with zero disclosure at the verdict line (the `open_source_constraints_deferrals` list stays empty per its own doc comment 'Empty list when the verdict is not PASS_WITH_OPEN_SOURCE_CONSTRAINTS').

All cited evidence (line numbers, printed strings, issue tags #608/#675) checks out exactly as described. The technical claim is accurate, and I found additional code (the _OPEN_SOURCE_CONTAINER_BLOCKED_STEPS[11] entry) showing this bypasses a mechanism the codebase already built for precisely this failure mode. verify.note:
Core claim independently re-verified as TRUE against current source (not just the description).

Confirmed via direct read of /home/reyerchu/vibe-ic-wt-final/vibe-ic-marketplace/plugins/vibe-ic/programs/flow_compliance_check.py:
- `_STRUCTURAL_RTL_GATES` is an AST-parsed tuple of exactly 242 elements (line 250-1459) — matches the finding's "242" figure exactly.
- `_run_structural_rtl_gates()` (def at line 3880, dispatch loop ~4076-4109): each gate worker returns "pass"/"fail"/"skip"/"waiver"; the "pass" branch (line 4104) appends nothing to fails/skips/waivers. Returns `(len(fails)==0), fails, skips, waivers`.
- Caller (line 6356-6413): `structural_result: Optional[StepResult] = None` is set, and the ONLY branch that constructs it is `if s_fails or s_skips or s_waivers:` (actual line 6367, finding said 6365 — off by 2). When all three lists are empty (all 242 gates cleanly PASS, no class-skips, no analog-skips, no waivers), this branch is skipped and `structural_result` stays None.
- Lines 6416-6417: `if structural_result is not None: results.append(structural_result)` — confirms None is never appended.
- Verified downstream: the per-step print loop (line 6611 `for r in results:`, emits the `✓/✗ [STATUS] Step <id>: ...` lines seen in real logs) and the JSON step list (`"steps": [asdict(r) for r in results]`, line ~6911) both iterate `results` only — so in the all-pass case, P0 is entirely absent from both the printed report and the JSON, not merely unlabeled.
- I wrote a standalone repro (monkeypatching `_run_structural_rtl_gates` to return `(True, [], [], [])` and replaying the exact caller condition) — confirmed `structural_result` stays None, printed at /tmp/.../scratchpad/repro_p0.py.
- Confirmed on the remote real run (ssh 192.168.1.120, ~/campaign_pr427/spm/converge_ihp-sg13g2/reports/audit/flow_compliance_check.log): P0 had 2 FAILs and 40+ SKIP lines (finding said "~20+", actual count is higher but the qualitative claim — real run never hit the all-empty case — holds), so P0 did construct and appear; the all-pass edge case is indeed not exercised by the cited real run, consistent with the LOW severity / "likely unreachable for realistic IC classes" characterization.

One inaccuracy found in the evidence field itself (does not invalidate the core claim): the quoted text "the marker is still suppressed because nothing to verify" does exist verbatim in the file, but at lines 6430-6431, NOT at "6348-6350" as cited — and it describes a distinct mechanism (the YAML-driven "P0" step-list entry being unconditionally filtered out of `_eval_steps` at lines 6435-6438, a documentation-only marker separate from the in-process `structural_result` umbrella). The actual comment at 6348-6350 says "P0 still appears first in the report because the umbrella result is prepended" — which doesn't discuss the all-pass edge case at all. So that specific citation is a sourcing error (wrong location + conflates two adjacent-but-different suppression mechanisms), and the line "6365" should be "6367". These are citation-precision issues, not fabrications of the underlying behavior — the core mechanism (silent disappearance of P0 on all-pass) is real and independently reproduced above.

Recommend keeping the finding but correcting the line number to 6367 and either dropping or relocating the misattributed quote citation.

refuted.summary: A second A7 checker (analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check.py) with an incompatible schema is what the runner's own internal per-step gate and P0 actually use, while the yaml step gate wires a different, documentation-mismatched checker -- the two disagree on the identical artifact.
refuted.evidence: analog_one_shot_runner.py:425 maps A7_post_layout_resim to programs/analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check.py (expects specs list of pre_value/post_value pairs), also registered in flow_compliance_check.py _STRUCTURAL_RTL_GATES line 330. The yaml A7 step gate (line 1036) instead wires analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check (expects comparisons or specs with pre/post keys). Reproduced: the exact stub JSON analog_one_shot_runner.py emits for A7 (lines 348-356, keys pre_value/post_value) produces PASS/rc=0 under analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check.py but FAIL/rc=1 (PRE_VS_POST_ZERO_COMPARED) under analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check.py.

verify.note:
Reproduced the low-level facts exactly, but the finding's central diagnostic claim about P0 is wrong.

CONFIRMED (matches the finding verbatim):
- analog_one_shot_runner.py:425 maps step A7_post_layout_resim -> programs/analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check.py, and the stub it emits at lines 348-356 uses keys `pre_value`/`post_value`.
- flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml:1036 wires the A7 step gate to `analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check` instead, which expects `comparisons`/`specs` items keyed `pre_layout`/`pre` and `post_layout`/`post`.
- I independently built the exact stub JSON (block dir under phase3/analog/<block>/pre_vs_post.json, per _path_layout.analog_dir) and ran both checkers directly:
  - analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check.py -> "PASS ... 1/1 block(s) clean", rc=0
  - analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check.py -> "[FAIL] ... PRE_VS_POST_ZERO_COMPARED: 0 specs were compared", rc=1
  This confirms the two checkers disagree on the identical artifact, exactly as claimed.

REFUTED PART: the claim that "P0 actually use[s]" the lenient A7 checker (implying P0 is fooled the same way the yaml-vs-runner mismatch would suggest) is factually wrong. flow_compliance_check.py's `_STRUCTURAL_RTL_GATES` tuple -- the actual list `_run_structural_rtl_gates()` iterates to build the P0 umbrella step (confirmed at line 6356/6406, `StepResult(id="P0", name=f"Structural-RTL gates (P0 umbrella, {len(_STRUCTURAL_RTL_GATES)} checkers)", ...)`) -- contains BOTH checker names as two independent, separately-dispatched gates over the same file:
  - line 312: "analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check" (the yaml-step-gate's strict checker)
  - line 330: "analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check" (the runner's per-step lenient checker)
Each gate is run via `prog = PROGRAMS_DIR / f"{gate_name}.py"` in the P0 loop, and P0's overall verdict is `len(fails) == 0` across ALL of them. Neither gate name appears in `_P0_THIN_INPUT_DEFERRABLE_SUBGATES` (the waiver/deferral allowlist), so a FAIL from analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check is a hard P0 FAIL, not softened. So on the exact stub artifact the finding cites, P0 does NOT silently pass -- it independently fails via its own direct invocation of the same strict checker the yaml step gate uses.

The real, much narrower defect is: the runner's own internal per-step status for A7 (used for progression/reporting inside analog_one_shot_runner.py) relies solely on the lenient checker and could locally report a false "A7: PASS" -- but that is not the same claim as "P0 actually uses" the lenient checker to the exclusion of the strict one, and P0 (the actual gating umbrella, confirmed used in the real flow_compliance_check.py main flow) is not fooled by this stub. I also checked the cited real-run project (ssh reyerchu@192.168.1.120, ~/campaign_pr427/spm/converge_ihp-sg13g2): it has no analog/pre_vs_post.json or A7 step artifacts at all, so the disagreement is a code-level construction, not something observed in that real run.

Given the finding's headline conclusion (P0 is misled into a false pass by the schema mismatch) does not hold under independent verification -- P0 has its own redundant, correctly-failing gate on the same artifact -- I'm marking this refuted. A corrected, narrower finding would be: "analog_one_shot_runner.py's per-step A7 status uses a lenient/incompatible checker that can diverge from the stricter checker P0 independently also runs on the same artifact; this can cause the runner's own progression/reporting to show a locally misleading A7 PASS even though P0 still correctly fails the project overall" -- LOW severity (reporting/consistency issue), not MEDIUM "P0 uses the wrong checker."

refuted.summary: analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check has no deterministic-stub or fabricated-data detection, unlike its A3/A4/A5/A8 sibling gates.
refuted.evidence: programs/analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check.py contains no import of _analog_stub_marker.is_stub_text and no provenance field check anywhere in the file (confirmed by full-file read), whereas analog_netlist_pdk_check.py, analog_a4_corner_sweep_check.py, and analog_hardmacro_check.py all explicitly detect and special-case a deterministic_stub marker. A fabricated pre_vs_post.json with suspiciously clean near-identical pre/post values (e.g. the runner's own A7 stub: pre_value 1.0, post_value 0.99) is indistinguishable from a genuine post-layout resimulation to this gate.

verify.note:
Re-ran everything independently against /home/reyerchu/vibe-ic-wt-final/vibe-ic-marketplace/plugins/vibe-ic/.

CODE-STRUCTURE CLAIM — CONFIRMED TRUE:
grep -n -i "stub|provenance" programs/analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check.py returns nothing (exit 1). Full read confirms: no import of _analog_stub_marker.is_stub_text, no `_provenance`/`deterministic_stub` field check anywhere in the file. By contrast analog_netlist_pdk_check.py (imports is_stub_text, PASS_WITH_STUB tier), analog_a4_corner_sweep_check.py (explicit `_provenance == "deterministic_stub"` rejection, v1.6.214 anti-stub gate), and analog_hardmacro_check.py (imports is_stub_text, PASS_WITH_STUB tier) all do have this. So the code-fact half of the finding is accurate.

CENTRAL EVIDENTIARY CLAIM — DOES NOT REPRODUCE, IN FACT REPRODUCES THE OPPOSITE:
The finding's proof point is: "the runner's own A7 stub: pre_value 1.0, post_value 0.99 ... is indistinguishable from a genuine post-layout resimulation to this gate" (i.e. implies it PASSes). I extracted the exact stub dict analog_one_shot_runner.py emits for A7 (lines 348-356: `{"specs": [{"name": "vout_v", "pre_value": 1.0, "post_value": 0.99}], ...}`) and ran it through the actual program:

  python3 analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check.py <dir-with-that-exact-stub>
  → [FAIL] PRE_VS_POST_ZERO_COMPARED, exit 1

It FAILS, not passes — for an unrelated reason: this checker only recognizes keys `pre_layout`/`post_layout` or `pre`/`post` (`item.get("pre_layout", item.get("pre"))`), but the runner (and every real pre_vs_post.json I found — the checker's own SKILL.md doc example, and a genuine campaign artifact at reyerchu@192.168.1.120:~/vibe-ic-wt-spm166/.../ldo/pre_vs_post.json) all use `pre_value`/`post_value` under a `specs` list. I ran the real remote artifact through the same checker and it ALSO fails with PRE_VS_POST_ZERO_COMPARED. So this gate currently blanket-fails essentially all real-world-shaped pre_vs_post.json (genuine or fake) via a schema mismatch — it is not silently passing fabricated data as the finding's example claims; if anything it's the opposite failure mode (false-FAIL on genuine data too).

I could construct a fabricated file that DOES pass cleanly (keys renamed to `pre`/`post`: `{"specs":[{"name":"vout_v","pre":1.0,"post":0.99}]}` → [PASS], exit 0), so the underlying "no stub detection lets near-identical fake data through" vulnerability class is real in the abstract — just not via the specific example cited.

ALSO: this file may not even be "the A7 gate" the finding thinks it is. analog_one_shot_runner.py's GATE_PROGRAMS dict wires the A7 step to a DIFFERENT file, analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check.py (not analog_pre_vs_post_layout_check.py — that one is an older, unprefixed, parallel gate also in flow_compliance_check.py's structural-gate list). analog_a7_post_layout_resim_check.py also has zero stub/provenance grep hits, but it cross-checks the linked A4 corner_results.json's `simulator_run` flag: when I fed it the runner's real combined A4+A7 stub pair (A4 stub has `simulator_run: false`), it correctly force-FAILed with A7_POSTSIM_NO_A4_SIM — it DOES catch the runner's own stub chain, just via upstream provenance-tracing rather than a marker in pre_vs_post.json itself. It only silently PASSes a fabricated pre_vs_post.json when there's no corresponding A4 evidence file to check against.

Conclusion: the narrow code-fact ("this specific file imports no stub-marker/provenance check, unlike those three named sibling files") is true, but the finding's headline impact claim/proof example is empirically false — I reproduced the opposite outcome from the one asserted, and the file the finding names is arguably not even the operative A7 gate in the real pipeline. Marking refuted given the central evidentiary example fails to reproduce.

verify.note:
Independently re-verified and REFUTED. I re-read flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml lines 1088-1107 locally and confirmed the finding's literal quote of the gate block (required_outputs=[phase2/stage2/synth/netlist.v]; gate.all_of has only two optional_program_exit_zero yosys-script checkers, no files_exist sub-gate) — that part is accurate as a description of the YAML step-level gate. I also read yosys_hilomap_required_check.py and yosys_script_template_check.py in full and confirmed neither inspects netlist.v (both are static auditors of .ys script text / command ordering only). BUT the finding's conclusion ('no mechanism anywhere ... verifies its own declared required_output actually exists' / 'a synth run that crashed before write_verilog would still VACUOUS_PASS/PASS this gate') is false, because it never looked past the YAML gate block into the consuming engine.

programs/flow_compliance_check.py:check_step() (the canonical compliance engine that consumes this flow yaml) runs a UNIVERSAL required_outputs presence check for every step, via `_glob_first(project, pattern)` against the real filesystem, BEFORE it ever evaluates the step's `gate` predicate (see lines ~5680-5698, with the hard early-return at ~5744 when `outputs and not result.evidence`). This is not step-14-specific code — it applies to all steps identically, and step 14 hits it like any other.

I reproduced this live rather than trusting the static read: built a synthetic project dir with phase2/stage2/synth/synth.ys containing a fully well-ordered techmap→hilomap→write_verilog script (which would pass both yosys checkers) but with netlist.v deliberately absent (simulating the exact 'crashed before write_verilog' scenario the finding describes), then called `flow_compliance_check.check_step(project, step14, {})` directly (imported the real module, parsed the real flow yaml, extracted the real step-14 dict). Result: `status == 'MISSING'`, reason `"no required_outputs found (expected: ['phase2/stage2/synth/netlist.v'])"` — NOT PASS or VACUOUS_PASS. Control test with netlist.v written back: status == 'PASS'. This directly contradicts the finding's claimed failure scenario.

verify.note:
Independently re-verified against both the local repo and the actual deployed plugin used for the real run (/home/reyerchu/.claude/plugins/cache/vibe-ic-marketplace/vibe-ic/1.6.71-pr427, confirmed via launch.sh/launch_phase3.sh on 192.168.1.120).

- Fresh flow_compliance_check.py run on ~/campaign_pr427/spm/converge_ihp-sg13g2 shows Step 29 = SKIPPED-CONDITION (canonical output absent, but a co-located sibling file sdf_sim_skipped.json self-reports a disclosed cap-gap skip, verdict=SKIPPED-CONDITION) and Step 31 = PASS.
- _SIGNOFF_RE does NOT match Step 29's name "Post-Layout Gate-Level Simulation (Post-Sim + SDF)" (verified via regex.search directly).

The finding's CENTRAL CAUSAL CLAIM is false, disproven by direct code execution:
1. "_SIGNOFF_RE ... is the only code that ever cross-checks blocks_on ancestry" is wrong. flow_step_execution_coverage_check.py has a PRIMARY graph-based check (analyze(), lines ~172-194) that walks the FULL transitive blocks_on ancestry via _ancestors() for EVERY step with status PASS/VACUOUS-PASS — not gated by _SIGNOFF_RE at all for the base walk.
2. "_SIGNOFF_RE ... only guards TERMINAL hand-off steps" is wrong. I ran m.analyze() with the real compliance report and the real graph (_load_blocks_on(Path('flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml'))) after manually setting Step 29's status to MISSING to simulate the finding's premise ("genuinely missing required outputs"), and the checker correctly fired: ordering_violations=[{'terminal_id': 31, 'terminal': 'Physical Verification...', 'signoff_id': 29, 'signoff_status': 'MISSING'}], verdict=FAIL. Step 31 is not a terminal hand-off step (doesn't match _TERMINAL_RE: gdsii/foundry-handoff/tapeout-checklist) — yet the graph check still enforced the dependency on it. This directly falsifies "only guards TERMINAL hand-off steps."
3. The regex non-match is causally irrelevant here: _SIGNOFF_RE is used inside the primary check ONLY to decide whether a VACUOUS-PASS ancestor should still be treated as blocking (line ~190-193). Step 29's actual status is SKIPPED-CONDITION, which is unconditionally exempted at the _NOT_APPLICABLE check (line ~182) BEFORE the VACUOUS-PASS/_SIGNOFF_RE branch is ever reached. So even if the regex did match Step 29's name, the outcome (no violation flagged) would be identical.

Root cause of the real behavior: flow_compliance_check.py classifies Step 29 as SKIPPED-CONDITION (a disclosed, self-reported capability-gap skip via sdf_sim_skipped.json, ticket #437d), and the coverage checker is deliberately designed to treat SKIPPED-CONDITION ancestors as legitimate for ANY downstream step (this is used identically and correctly across dozens of steps: A6, M1-M4, 40-44, etc.) — not a code gap unique to Step 29/31 or attributable to a regex miss. Whether Step 29's SKIPPED-CONDITION classification is itself an appropriate methodology choice is a separate, legitimate question from the one the finding actually argues (a code-enforcement gap caused by a specific regex not matching), and that specific mechanistic claim is empirically disproven.

Given the finding's supporting evidence about the code mechanism is factually incorrect (verified by direct execution/instrumentation, not just re-reading), I judge this finding refuted.

Full flow_compliance_check.py run against the real project (synced full plugin tree so sibling-module imports resolve) reports step id 38 status="PASS" with evidence=[mask_spec.json, wat_plan.json, corner_test_vectors.json, foundry_handoff_audit.json] — scribe_line_layout.gds absent from evidence, as claimed.

So the raw evidence is 100% reproduced. But the finding's framing — "PASSes even though the required scribe-line GDS deliverable is genuinely absent," severity HIGH, implying an undetected/false-PASS gap — does not hold up once the design intent is checked, and I judge it refuted on that basis:

1. `foundry_handoff_package_check.py` deliberately excludes scribe_line_layout.gds from `_REQUIRED_FILES` (only mask_spec.json + wat_plan.json). Its v1.6.162 chip-GDS logic instead requires a real, non-empty, correctly-named CHIP GDS elsewhere (phase3/stage4/gds/), which IS present here: spm.gds, 881530 B, resolved and matched against L1.ic_name="spm" (confirmed in the JSON report: "chip_gds": ".../phase3/stage4/gds/spm.gds", "scribe_only": false).
2. The scribe_line_layout.gds absence is not silent/hidden: the directory carries scribe_line_layout.PENDING_FOUNDRY.txt and README.txt, both explicitly stating "scribe_line_layout.gds is FOUNDRY-SUPPLIED (PCM structures + alignment marks) and is NOT generated here (#446). Obtain it from the shuttle/foundry kit... before tapeout."
3. Git history shows this is a deliberate fix, not an oversight: commit 20cbee6b1 (v0.2.76, ORGANIC-20260606 #446) explicitly replaced an EARLIER, WORSE bug — a fabricated fake-content file literally named scribe_line_layout.gds — with this honest non-existence + disclosure pattern. Follow-on commits 97c3bcb67/09ef02a45 (#449) further hardened the "PENDING_FOUNDRY_* = honest open item, INFO not ERROR" semantics.
4. programs/tests/test_v0_2_81_pending_foundry_semantics.py pins exactly this behavior as correct: `test_fresh_generator_output_passes_own_gate` asserts a fresh pack (which also omits scribe_line_layout.gds) returns rc=0/PASS with pending_foundry_fields listed as INFO — i.e., this is regression-tested intended behavior, not an unnoticed gap.
5. The yaml's step-38 `required_outputs` list does name scribe_line_layout.gds, but flow_compliance_check.py's required_outputs check is an any-of check (fails only if ALL listed outputs are absent), and the actual PASS/FAIL determinant is the `gate.program_exit_zero` call to foundry_handoff_package_check.py, which by design doesn't gate on this specific file for the reasons above.

One real but much narrower observation I'd flag separately (not what this finding claims, and not HIGH severity): the machine-readable reports/phase3/foundry_handoff_audit.json's `pending_foundry_fields` list only enumerates in-JSON PENDING_FOUNDRY_* keys, not the scribe_line_layout.gds file-level absence itself as a named structured entry — so a consumer reading only that JSON (not the directory's .txt/README) wouldn't see the scribe-line item named there. That's a minor report-completeness nit, not the "genuine defect / false PASS" HIGH-severity claim in the finding as written, so I'm marking the finding refuted overall.

refuted.summary: The 4th M2 sub-check's own JSON report path is not declared in required_outputs.
refuted.evidence: flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml gate line 1908 runs power_domain_signal_crossing_check with `--json reports/phase2/gates/power_domain_signal_crossing.json`, but required_outputs (lines 1894-1897) lists only power_domain.json, level_shifter.json, isolation.json — the 4th check's own artefact is absent from the list.

verify.note: Literal citation checks out (re-read flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml locally): line 1908 is `power_domain_signal_crossing_check . --json reports/phase2/gates/power_domain_signal_crossing.json`, and required_outputs at 1894-1897 lists only power_domain.json / level_shifter.json / isolation.json. But the finding's inference is wrong. Read the 3 sibling check programs (power_domain_crossing_check.py, level_shifter_required_check.py, isolation_cell_required_check.py): power_domain.json/level_shifter.json/isolation.json are INPUT sidecar files these checks READ (produced upstream, not by M2), while each check WRITES its own distinct audit report via --json (power_domain_crossing_audit.json, level_shifter_audit.json, isolation_audit.json) that is likewise absent from required_outputs. So it is false that "3 of the 4 checks' own artefacts are declared and only the 4th is missing" — none of the 4 checks' own report paths are in required_outputs; the listed files are unrelated pre-existing dependencies. Also read gate_self_assertion_check.py, the actual consumer that cares whether a file is in required_outputs: it flags a step only when a `json_field_true` predicate trusts a file the SAME step lists in required_outputs with no program_exit_zero backing it. M2's gate uses only program_exit_zero predicates (no json_field_true), so this concern doesn't even apply. To confirm this is the codebase norm and not an M2-specific defect, I scripted a full scan of flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml: of 72 program_exit_zero --json paths across all steps, only 11 (15%) appear in that step's required_outputs; 61 do not (steps 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, FS1, DT1 all show multiple sibling checks whose own audit paths are absent from required_outputs, same shape as M2). required_outputs is a distinct "primary deliverable / evidence-presence" concept consumed by flow_compliance_check.py, flow_dashboard_data.py, flow_step_executor_coverage_check.py, and flow_condition_reachability_check.py — not an enumeration of every gate sub-check's own report file. On the remote real run (192.168.1.120:~/campaign_pr427/spm/converge_ihp-sg13g2), M2 is status='na' (no phase1/analog/analog_block_list.json — pure digital design), so the gate never even executed there. Conclusion: the cited lines are real, but the "gap" is the pervasive, apparently intentional pattern throughout this YAML, not an anomaly unique to M2's 4th sub-check, and no actual consumer of required_outputs depends on it including this path. Refuting as a false positive / non-issue.

refuted.summary: Step 43's blocks_on:[42] dependency is not enforced anywhere in check_step, so it can report PASS while step 42 (Packaging) is genuinely MISSING.
refuted.evidence: Reproduced with programs/flow_compliance_check.py's check_step() directly: synthetic project has phase3/stage5_manufacturing/silicon_received.json + a valid final_test_yield.json (measured 98% >= target 95%), but packaging_log.json (step 42's sole required_output) is completely absent. Result: step 42 = MISSING ('no required_outputs found'), step 43 = PASS with zero reasons. blocks_on is only consumed later by _attribute_cascade_verdicts() (flow_compliance_check.py:5920), which merely relabels already-MISSING steps for reporting attribution — it never revokes an independently-reached PASS.

verify.note: Reproduced check_step() in isolation exactly as the finding describes: step42=MISSING, step43=PASS with zero reasons — that narrow claim is accurate. But the finding's headline conclusion is false: flow_compliance_check.py's actual main() entry point (lines 6687-6716) unconditionally invokes flow_step_execution_coverage_check.py, which walks the same blocks_on graph and explicitly catches any PASS/VACUOUS-PASS step whose blocks_on ancestor is MISSING/FAIL. Running the real CLI on the exact synthetic project described (silicon_received.json + valid final_test_yield.json, no packaging_log.json) produces 'Overall: FAIL' with the explicit line '[43] Final Test ... = PASS marked done while dependency [42] Packaging ... = MISSING'. This guard is not gated by any CLI flag. I also confirmed the identical guard exists in the exact remote real-run plugin version cited (1.6.71-pr427 at ~/.claude/plugins/cache/vibe-ic-marketplace/vibe-ic/1.6.71-pr427 on 192.168.1.120, used by campaign_pr427/spm/converge_ihp-sg13g2's launch.sh). The finding cherry-picked check_step()+_attribute_cascade_verdicts() and omitted this dedicated ordering-enforcement module, making its 'not enforced anywhere' / HIGH-severity claim materially misleading about the tool's actual reported output.
